perspective:
From Mason Hurley’s available perspective:

- Mason is an accountant at a small community center. Martha Moua is a personal care aide there. They are colleagues with a professional, not close, relationship and interact mainly about work.
- Mason reviewed the community center’s financial reports and noticed discrepancies: healthcare expenses seemed unusually high and did not align with usual spending patterns. This made him suspicious and anxious, and he suspected Martha might be mismanaging funds.
- Mason asked Martha to discuss the recent financial report. He told her some numbers did not add up and pointed specifically to the healthcare expense section. He heard Martha say there might have been a misentry, that she would review it, and that she would correct any errors.
- After reviewing the report with Martha and hearing her clarification, Mason concluded the discrepancies were due to a simple clerical error, not mismanagement. He felt relieved but embarrassed. He apologized to Martha for his initial suspicion. He heard Martha say errors happen, she was glad they cleared it up quickly, she understood he was being thorough, and they should double-check entries next time.
- Mason then believed Martha was competent, but thought the recurring clerical errors showed the financial management system was inadequate. He felt frustrated with the system but empathetic toward Martha.
- Mason suggested preventing future errors by proposing a new, more robust financial system. He said he would draft a proposal and wanted Martha’s input. He heard Martha agree, say it sounded like a great idea, and offer to help address the identified gaps.
- Mason finished drafting the new financial system proposal. He believed it would benefit operations but was uncertain whether management would approve or implement it. He told Martha this. He heard Martha say it was a solid proposal, to present it confidently, and that the benefits were clear. Mason asked her to help gather data to strengthen their case; she agreed.
- Mason presented the proposal to management. He felt satisfied with his efforts but physically and mentally exhausted, believing he had done everything he could. He told Martha the presentation went well and that it was now up to management. He heard Martha praise his work, suggest taking time off, and offer help while he was away.
- Mason said he would take a few days off to recharge and reflect, hoping they would return to good news. He heard Martha wish him a good break and tell him to let her know if he needed anything while away.
